root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `sudoers_parse_ldif()` may enter `ldif_to_sudoers(parse_tree, &roles, numroles, store_options)`, it must prove that at least one completed role was collected (`numroles > 0`).
root_cause_criterion.description: The selected root obligation is the non-empty-role guard at the conversion call site. On the saved malformed-LDIF witness, no completed `sudoRole` is inserted, so `numroles` remains 0 and the vulnerable original still enters `ldif_to_sudoers()`.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The vulnerable original violates the frozen predicate while reaching the protected sink event. The fixed original is guarded on the saved six-byte witness. Two adjacent fixed perturbations (`single_role_boundary` and `single_role_long_cn`) flip `numroles` to 1, but both builds still crash earlier at `parse_ldif.c:488` before the protected sentinel-write event executes, so `assertion_results.json` records the unresolved differential failure.

nodes.state: At the faulting sentinel write, `n == numroles`, and on the crashing original both values are 0, so the first write through `role_array` occurs immediately after the zero-iteration copy loop.

edges.relation: The same zero `numroles` value that should have blocked the conversion call is carried unchanged into `ldif_to_sudoers()` and is still the role-count operand when the sentinel write executes.
